jumps.name: Q3 2026 earnings release (Oct 16, 2026)
jumps.reason: Q3 results are a binary event for a stock trading near its bank-appropriate fair value; quarterly earnings reactions have historically produced large MTB moves in either direction.
jumps.cite: evaluation Bear case: 'Q3 results on Oct 16 are a binary event [Certain]'; fact sheet Price 'Next earnings date: Oct 16, 2026 (ST,OV)'.

annual_probability.cite: 2 of ~20 quarterly earnings weeks since 2021 exceeded 10% in magnitude (2022-01-18 -13.61%, 2022-10-17 -12.82%; mc-inputs analogues.event_weeks). Scaled to 4 earnings/yr: 4x(2/20)=0.4 expected large-reaction events/yr; P(>=1 in 12m) = 1-e^-0.4 ≈ 0.33.

impact.cite: Matches the analogue week exactly (mc-inputs analogues.event_weeks: 2022-10-17, Q3 2022 earnings release, move -0.1282).

jumps.name: Office CRE / criticized-loan credit deterioration
jumps.reason: Management flagged an elevated and rising share of criticized office CRE loans, with further downgrades expected over the next one to two years, a risk not yet visible in stockanalysis.com's aggregate credit metrics.
jumps.cite: research note section 6 'Unusual items': 'M&T carries meaningful commercial real estate exposure, including an office book where management flagged an elevated share of criticized loans and expects further downgrades over the next one to two years' (Q2 2026 call, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mtb/transcripts/649590-q2-2026/); evaluation Bear case 'Office CRE criticized loans are expected to rise over 1-2 years'.

annual_probability.cite: Management's own one-to-two-year horizon for further downgrades (Q2 2026 call) implies roughly a 1-in-3 to 1-in-2 chance of this crystallizing into a market-moving credit event in any given year; taken as 30%/yr.

impact.cite: No analogue; impact assumed per 'assumption' field below, within the ±30% bound for assumptions.

jumps.assumption: No single week in MTB's 5y weekly history (mc-inputs analogues) isolates a CRE/office credit event specifically, so no analogue is used. Impact is assumed at -15%, inside the ±30% max_jump_impact_assumed bound, scaled below the largest non-earnings weekly falls observed in the history (-13.65% proxy week 2023-03-06, -10.42% 2025-03-31) because this is a gradual provisioning/credit-quality risk rather than a single-week shock.
